dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: Arana will take care of her. She is a most cherished friend.

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, please go to Vanarana and sing the Rhythm of the Great Dream. Then ask them to help prepare the Bija.

choices.text: I'm not sure I understand you...

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Like clouds know they have to release rain, rain knows they need to fall onto ground, and seeds know they need to grow into big trees and have lots of big fruits.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, it looks like you don't understand. It's okay. When the right time comes, Nara {NICKNAME} will know what to do.

choices.text: (I have to help Rana recover soon...)

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: (Rana is still sleeping. Arana is not around.)

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: (A blurry image appears in the "bubble" that envelopes Rana.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You are in a forest where everything looks incomparably massive and serene. You feel very comfortable here.\nRays of sunshine peek through the sparkling gold leaves, with grass as tall as you swaying quietly all around, gently caressing your hand as you walk by.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You hear the sound of distressed crying amid the musical melody of the wind blowing through the trees and flowing water. Following the sound, you find a small girl.\nShe looks like she has worn herself out from crying and fallen asleep in the meadow. You walk up to her and softly sing a song that can calm all beings...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: (... It seems that Rana's condition hasn't worsened.)

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: (Rana is still sleeping. She should be fine since Arana's Ararakalari is here.)

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Oh, it's Nara {NICKNAME}. Do you have any questions for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you need a hand with anything?

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Oh, thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}. As you can see, I'm doing rather well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are any Aranara in need of help?

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Oh, well... Go to the center of Vanarana, and you should see Arapacati there. Something has been troubling her lately.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything else to be done for Festival Utsava?

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: About that, Arakavi should be at the center of Vanarana. I think he's also in need of help for Festival Utsava.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About "Marana"...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: That's a story from very long ago...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: A long time ago, Aranara walked the earth and made friends with Nara and all living creatures. There was no Marana then. Until a disaster that occurred many, many moons ago...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata returned to Sarva, and the Marana's rampage through the earth began. Once the forest recovered its vitality, the Aranara hid the real Vanarana in a dream to protect themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: The forest didn't know death, until a day came when the trees realized that withered flowers and dead animals covered the earth.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: On the same day, the earth remembered the dark, poisonous blood it had once devoured, or was about to devour. The rivers thought of the descent of the sun, evaporating all water and leaving a red world behind.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: They realized that all things would meet their end, and so, Marana was born. It is the name of death, and those who know it shall die.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Marana urges everything towards death. As for the tall, dark, and warped beings, they are the avatars chosen by Marana, the heralds of death.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Of course. In my stories, Marana's Avatar takes many forms. Sometimes beasts, sometimes birds, sometimes Nara, sometimes blight...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: But stories are just stories, and they aren't my memories.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Vasoma Fruit...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: It's a fruit full of energy. It grows on the memories and dreams in the earth, and it needs the help of Aranara and Nara to bear fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: A Bija can be formed by feeding a Vasoma Fruit to the Ashvattha Tree. It's a great tree planted by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, and it's the origin of Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Aranyaka...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #It belonged to Nara Varuna. {M#She}{F#He} was a Golden Nara who was kind, brave, and honest, just like you.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #I still remember how the Aranara of that time missed {M#her}{F#him} and loved {M#her}{F#his} stories. But I believe that since Nara {NICKNAME} is here now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Yes. I look forward to celebrating Festival Utsava with you.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: I can't thank you enough for preparing Festival Utsava.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: It's a pity that I couldn't join your adventures like Arama and the others, nor was I able to provide any help.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: That being said, if you ever feel tired during your adventures, come visit Vanarana. You're always welcomed in this dream.
